title: Suggestions for review — pick a path before anything is implemented
workflow: 1) Read the suggestion, its options and its evidence. 2) Write a verdict naming exactly one option. 3) Only then is code written against it. Nothing on this page is implemented by default, and the verdict column starts blank.
ordering: P0 = unblocks other work or prevents a wrong publication; P1 = high value, mild dependency; P2 = valuable once the P0s are decided.

rows.title: Choose the price source, or formally give up on the residual
rows.problem: Three requirements (price snapshots, fair/market/difference, CLV) and every ROI number share one missing input: a market price. Today 39 of 39 snapshot rows have a fair value and 0 have a market value. Every staking figure uses an assumed -110.

options.label: License a sportsbook or data-vendor feed
options.effect: Closes G7 and unblocks A01-A03, C06, F09. Costs money and needs republication terms in writing.
options.risk: Terms may forbid republishing the numbers, which would leave the site unable to show its own residuals.

options.label: Stay price-free and rename the product
options.effect: Zero legal exposure. The site publishes fair lines and skill scores only, and the market and difference columns are removed rather than left permanently blank.
options.risk: No CLV, no ROI, no rewards. The competition becomes a proper-score contest, which Q08 may actually prefer.

options.label: Publish a clearly-labelled non-market baseline
options.effect: Publish '#our fair line vs a fixed reference' instead of vs the market, e.g. vs the previous week's published fair line. Honest, immediately computable, and it measures model stability rather than market edge.
options.risk: Someone will read it as an edge. The label has to be loud.

rows.evidence: Week 11 schedule page publishes kickoff, network and venue for 13 fixtures and no line at all. Flags FB-01/FB-02 record the consequence.
rows.cost: A: procurement + legal. B: a page edit. C: one day.
rows.risk: A is the only path to the requirements as written. B and C are honest retreats.
rows.recommendation: A if the budget exists; otherwise C, because C keeps a daily publishing habit alive and is the only option that produces a number every week.

rows.title: Make the decision-readiness table the site's front door
rows.problem: Nineteen NFL site trees exist and a twentieth is added by every new session. The owner has no single place that says what is blocked and by how much.

options.label: Decision-readiness page becomes the canonical landing page
options.effect: One front door. Every other namespace becomes archive, linked but not authoritative.
options.risk: Feels like throwing away peer work; it is not, the work stays reachable.

options.label: Keep the current landing page and link the table from it
options.effect: Lower risk to existing navigation. The table becomes one more link among 179.
options.risk: The problem recurs on the next session; links are what already failed.

options.label: Freeze new namespaces until the table has no unclaimed P0 row
options.effect: Stops the sprawl at the cause instead of the symptom.
options.risk: Slows parallel work, which is this repository's actual working style.

rows.evidence: 26 namespaces on main; the root nav generator already carries a comment about links being silently dropped by regeneration.
rows.cost: A: hours. B: minutes. C: governance only.
rows.risk: A and C together are the only combination that holds.
rows.recommendation: A now, then C as a standing rule.

rows.title: Ingest the official inactives article — it closes the biggest perceived dead end
rows.problem: The repository treats the active list as unobtainable. It is obtainable. nfl.com publishes a dated article naming every inactive player per club, and it also carries the venue string for each game.

options.label: Capture it weekly, starting now
options.effect: One page per week yields ~138 named inactives, 24 club sections and 12 venue strings. It is the cheapest evidence win available.
options.risk: Sunday Night Football lists publish ~90 minutes before kickoff, so a single capture will always be incomplete for the last game.

options.label: Capture it twice: once mid-afternoon, once after the SNF list publishes
options.effect: Complete coverage for all 12-16 Sunday clubs plus the primetime clubs.
options.risk: Doubles the job count for one source.

options.label: Wait until the Game Book pipeline exists
options.effect: Fewer moving parts.
options.risk: Freezes 20 of the 78 readiness rows on an unproven PDF pipeline.

rows.evidence: Week 10 article read in full this session: 24 sections, 138 named players, 12 venue strings, 2 empty lists priced by timing rather than absence.
rows.cost: A: one parser, a few hours. B: the same parser, two cron entries.
rows.risk: Low. The article is the most structured availability source found so far.
rows.recommendation: B. Take the capture twice and store the clock time; that also turns the report into the timestamped series E05 requires.

rows.title: Test one Game Book PDF before promising the availability graph
rows.problem: The requirements for 'who was expected to start, who actually did', a replacement-depth matrix and starter-level ablations all rest on knowing starters. The only official source for that is the Game Book.

options.label: Parse one Game Book now and publish the result either way
options.effect: A one-day experiment that either unlocks four requirements or rules them out.
options.risk: PDF tables are often positional rather than tagged, so a parse may need per-page coordinates.

options.label: Infer starters from the depth charts
options.effect: No PDF work.
options.risk: Forbidden by the brief, and only 1 of 32 clubs has a verified structured chart anyway.

options.label: Infer starters from snap counts
options.effect: Avoids PDFs.
options.risk: No official snap-count source was located, and the brief explicitly rejects inference here.

rows.evidence: Game centre for WAS@NYG Week 10 links 'Download Game Book (PDF)' at static.www.nfl.com. One link observed, zero parsed.
rows.cost: A: one day. B and C: unbounded, and disallowed.
rows.risk: A's downside is a day. B and C's downside is fabricated starters.
rows.recommendation: A, and publish the negative result if it fails. A known dead end is worth as much as a win here.

rows.title: Stop publishing counts that a live page can move
rows.problem: The brief itself quotes 254 rows and 4 no-injury sections, then 279 rows and 2 sections. Read today the page has 28 sections and 347 rows and no injury-free section at all. Three different numbers, all 'verified' on the day they were written.

options.label: Publish every count with its capture clock and never as a bare fact
options.effect: The number becomes falsifiable rather than stale.
options.risk: Verbose cells.

options.label: Publish only diffs against the previous capture
options.effect: Impossible to quote a stale absolute.
options.risk: Needs two captures, so it must wait for the archive.

options.label: Pin the count in CI so the build fails when it moves
options.effect: Turns a silent drift into a red build, which is what D07 asks for.
options.risk: A live page will break the build on a normal Tuesday, so the pin has to be an expected-range, not an equality.

rows.evidence: This session's full 8-of-8-chunk read: 28 sections, 347 rows, 0 empty sections.
rows.cost: A: a template change. C: half a day.
rows.risk: Low; the failure mode of doing nothing is already visible in the brief's own numbers.
rows.recommendation: A now and C with a tolerance band. Skip B until the archive exists.

rows.title: Render 'not listed' as unknown, not available
rows.problem: 70 of 138 named inactives do not appear in the weekly injury report at all. A player absent from the report is invisible, and an invisible player currently reads as healthy.

options.label: Three-state availability: available / unavailable / unknown
options.effect: The report can only ever produce 'unavailable' and 'unknown'; only an active list produces 'available'.
options.risk: Most of the league becomes 'unknown' and the page looks empty.

options.label: Add the reserve list and treat report-absence as available only for players confirmed on an active roster
options.effect: Resolves most of the unknowns.
options.risk: Needs an official roster and reserve feed, which is not in hand.

options.label: Leave the binary rendering and add a footnote
options.effect: No work.
options.risk: A footnote is exactly what a model will not read. This is the defect the brief keeps flagging.

rows.evidence: 68 inactives join to the report; 70 do not. Malik Willis (MIA) appears in no Week 10 section, which is what an injured-reserve player looks like in this source.
rows.cost: A: half a day. B: depends on the roster feed.
rows.risk: An empty-looking page is a correct page.
rows.recommendation: A now, B when the roster feed lands.

rows.title: Re-freeze the backtest corpus with a published hash
rows.problem: Pre-registration says 136 games; the file now has 137. The registration and the artefact have drifted, which is the exact failure pre-registration exists to prevent.

options.label: Re-freeze at today's 137 with a commit hash on the strategy page
options.effect: Registration and artefact agree again from today.
options.risk: Re-freezing after seeing results is a soft form of peeking; the reason must be recorded.

options.label: Pin to the original 136 and exclude later games from the registered evaluation
options.effect: The registration stays honest and the extra game is used only for the live shadow.
options.risk: The corpus slowly becomes historical while the site claims it is live.

options.label: Re-define the corpus as 'all settled games as of the capture clock'
options.effect: No drift is possible, because the definition is the rule.
options.risk: Comparisons across weeks need the capture clock to be carried everywhere.

rows.evidence: results_feed.json n_games=137; own_lines_open.json n_train_games=136 and train_through_week=9.
rows.risk: A is the only option that quietly permits result-chasing. Say so in the log if it is chosen.
rows.recommendation: C for the live shadow, B for the one published backtest.

rows.title: Report a p-value of exactly zero as a resolution floor
rows.problem: 0 of 500 permutation draws is published as p=0. On n=105 forecasts that is arithmetically impossible as a true probability, and it reads as certainty.

options.label: Publish '< 0.002 (0/500)' and raise the draw count to 10,000 in the same run
options.effect: Honest and cheap. 10,000 draws bounds p at < 0.0001.
options.risk: Runtime, which is trivial at this n.

options.label: Add a second, independent season before publishing any p
options.effect: Solves the real problem, which is sample size, not formatting.
options.risk: Needs Q03's prior-season data.

options.label: Leave it; the flag already notes it
options.effect: No work.
options.risk: A reader sees p=0 and stops reading the flag.

rows.evidence: backtest.json placebo reports 0/500; flag FB-16 says the same thing but the page shows the number.
rows.recommendation: A immediately, B as the substantive fix.

rows.title: Make the verifier fail on a stale snapshot, not just a broken link
rows.problem: Both existing verifiers check links and sources. Neither notices that a standings snapshot has been overtaken by nine games.

options.label: Add an age field and fail the build past a threshold
options.effect: A stale table cannot ship silently.
options.risk: Threshold choice is arbitrary and needs an owner decision.

options.label: Add a re-read check that compares three randomly chosen rows against the live page
options.effect: Catches drift in content, not just in date.
options.risk: Makes CI depend on the live network, which is flaky.

options.label: Publish the capture clock prominently and let the reader judge
options.effect: Zero engineering.
options.risk: This is what already exists and it did not work.

rows.evidence: This session found the peer standings snapshot stale on all 32 clubs; flag FB-03/FB-04 already knew rows were partial.
rows.cost: A: an hour. B: a day plus flakiness.
rows.risk: B's flakiness is a real cost; a red build for a network blip trains people to ignore red.
rows.recommendation: A now. B only as a scheduled job, never as a PR gate.

rows.title: Give every strategy a falsifier, not just a threshold
rows.problem: A strategy currently has a rule and a threshold. Neither says what observation would retire it, so nothing can be demoted on evidence.

options.label: Two mandatory columns: promote-if and retire-if, each with a number
options.effect: The demotion gate gets something to fire on.
options.risk: Two more blanks per row until the data exists.

options.label: Derive the falsifier from the demotion gate automatically
options.effect: No authoring burden.
options.risk: The gate is generic, so the falsifier is generic and useless for a specific strategy.

options.label: Skip it; the demotion gate covers demotion
options.effect: No work.
options.risk: The gate covers 4 mechanical conditions and cannot express 'the thesis was wrong'.

rows.evidence: 5 strategies carry rule + threshold; 0 carry an explicit two-sided falsifier.

rows.title: Show the model's own uncertainty on every originated line
rows.problem: A fair line is published as a number. A reader cannot tell a 1-point estimate from a 6-point one.

options.label: Publish the fair line with a stated interval and the sd used
options.effect: The reader can see whether a difference is even resolvable.
options.risk: An interval invites false precision if the model is misspecified.

options.label: Publish only the interval width as a separate confidence column
options.effect: Cheaper, less pretentious.
options.risk: Harder to use.

options.label: Leave it; the model card carries the sd
options.effect: No work.
options.risk: The model card is a different page, and nobody joins pages by hand.

rows.evidence: model_card.json publishes sd_margin=10.454 and mu=22.959; own_lines pages publish point estimates only.

rows.title: Split schedule-derived features from stadium features instead of blocking both
rows.problem: The fixture-context requirement bundles buildable facts (rest days, travel, short week) with unbuildable ones (roof, surface, NWS weather) and therefore delivers nothing.

options.label: Ship the schedule half now, mark the stadium half blocked
options.effect: 13 of 13 Week 11 fixtures get rest-day and travel features from the schedule page alone.
options.risk: Half a feature set can look like a whole one.

options.label: Wait for the stadium source
options.effect: No risk of a partial feature being misread.
options.risk: Delivers nothing, possibly for a long time.

options.label: Substitute a third-party roof/surface table
options.effect: Unblocks immediately.
options.risk: It would not be an official source, which the brief forbids.

rows.evidence: Schedule page gives date, kickoff and network for 13 fixtures; no roof or surface appears on any page read this session.
rows.risk: Low if the labelling is explicit.

rows.title: Publish the questions register as the change-control document
rows.problem: Decisions get made in prose inside 26 namespaces. When a requirement changes, nothing records which question it answered.

options.label: Every closed question must name the commit that closed it
options.effect: A decision trail that survives sessions.
options.risk: Bookkeeping overhead on every task.

options.label: Leave it informal
options.effect: No overhead.
options.risk: The same questions get re-asked, which is already visible across the peer namespaces.

options.label: Fold the register into the readiness table
options.effect: One document instead of two.
options.risk: The table gets long.

rows.evidence: This repository has 6 executive summaries and 26 namespaces; the same price-source question appears in at least 5 of them.
